To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ITAI comprising the expression products of the MYC, E2F1 and p21 genes, accurately distinguishes normal BEC from malignant BEC.

stable two-fold upregulation of p21 TA in the malignant BEC line, A549, down-regulated E2F1 transcript abundance and restored cell proliferation control, as evidenced by reduced population doubling potential, increased population doubling time, and resumption of contact inhibition.
experimental up-regulation of p21 in A549 human lung carcinoma cells results in down-regulation of [MYC ×E2F1], loss of immortality, and restoration of limited cell population doubling capability.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an assay for the early detection of lung cancer, based on a bivariate transcript abundance index (TBI), which is comprised of three cell cycle control transcripts, [MYC x E2F1 ]/p21.
the identification of biomarkers that can be used to distinguish normal and malignant BECs.
the development and application of a novel, simple, quantitative method for identifying malignant BEC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the [MYC×E2F1]/ p21 index, with a cut-off of 7,00, is an effective tool to differentiate normal and malignant BECs at the transcript abundance.
the ITAI of 7,00 accurately quantifies the difference in transcript abundance between normal and malignant bronchial cells.
the [MYC x E2F1)/p21 ITAI is a quantitative biomarker of the malignant state in BEC, and that the ITAI is an important and potentially useful biomarker in the diagnosis and management of lung cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p21 versus E2F1 bivariate plot is the most accurate and reproducible method to quantify, at the level of TA, the difference between malignant and normal BEC.

a line with a 7,000 slope on a bivariate p21 versus [E2F1 × MYC] plot is a transcript abundance-based biomarker of BEC immortality, and that experimental up-regulation of p21 in A549 human lung adenocarcinoma cells down-regulates EGF1 mRNA and restores limited cell population doubling potential.
malignant bronchogenic carcinoma cells are characterized by deregulated cell cycle control at the level of transcription, and that this deregulation can be quantified at the level of mRNA abundance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple bivariate plot, with a cut-off line, can be used to quantitatively distinguish normal from malignant BEC at transcript abundance level.
the [MYC x E2F1/p21] ITAI accurately quantifies the difference in transcript abundance between normal and malignant bronchial cell lines.
the ITAI accurately distinguishes normal from malignant BEC, and can be used as an early detection biomarker for BEC.
